To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

hierarchical structure is a central organizing principal of complex networks, and can be used to simultaneously explain and reproduce many commonly observed network properties and also to predict missing links in networks.

(a) Hierarchical structure can be inferred from network data, (b) the existence of hierarchy explains many commonly observed topologies in networks, and (c) knowledge of hierarchical structure allows us to predict missing connections.

(i) networks can often be represented as hierarchical structures, in which vertices group together into communities that further subdivide over multiple scales, (ii) the existence of such hierarchical structure can simultaneously explain and predict many commonly observed topologies of complex networks, such as high clustering coefficients and right skewed degree distributions; and (iii) the hierarchical structure can be inferred from the network itself without any prior knowledge about functional units or community structure.
